sources.headline: 'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono
sources.text: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competition this week.Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on Wednesday, explaining the 25-year-old "wishes to share a few words personally"."These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono says in the statement."I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened."I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him."I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing."Rest in peace, Jesus."Earlier on Wednesday, FC Andorra team-mate Lautaro Spatz defended Owono and said he "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and had been "deeply affected" by De Miguel's death.Writing on social media, centre-back Spatz said Owono was devastated.Spatz paid tribute to De Miguel, then said of Owono: "Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone."In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."Players from FC Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono was not at the session.Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time on Monday when the incident occurred.Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him, before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.The goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.Police in Spain opened a routine investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.Owono has made 47 international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.The president of Equatorial Guinea's football federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, issued a statement on Tuesday offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player."As the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress," he added.On Tuesday, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.Tenerife said in a statement they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time.The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo.Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell"."Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the club statement.Tenerife and Andorra's Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend, against Granada and Mallorca respectively, have been postponed.

sources.headline: Owono enduring ‘hardest days of my life’ after De Miguel death
sources.text: Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries from a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono.FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday.The 30-year-old Spanish footballer died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in the collision with Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who had raced into midfield to clear an aerial ball.“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra on Wednesday.“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.”Spanish police sources told the AFP news agency that an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision.Andorra players observed a minute’s silence on Wednesday before a voluntary training session, which Owono, 25, did not attend.Owono received support from the president of the African country’s federation, Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, in a letter of condolence following De Miguel’s death.“I feel compelled to convey all our solidarity and support at this time to our player Jesus Lazaro Owono,” Micha wrote.“We know that, as the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress.“From the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation, we offer him all our human and professional backing, fully aware of the harshness of this event, which no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.”Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz posted on Instagram in support of Owono, whom he said was “deeply affected” by what had happened.“Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone,” wrote Spatz.“In football, unfortunate incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.”PostponementsEarlier on Wednesday, it was confirmed that Tenerife and Andorra’s Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend would be postponed.Tenerife were due to face Granada away from home, while Andorra were set to welcome Mallorca.“After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game … this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes [stadium], has been postponed,” said Granada in a statement.Mallorca said, “At times like this, respect and sensitivity in the face of a situation of profound grief must come first.”The Spanish football federation postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches this week as a mark of respect following De Miguel’s death.Tenerife plan to hold a tribute to De Miguel at the club’s stadium on Saturday, which supporters can attend, and are holding a six-day mourning period.The club said the first team, board and staff will attend De Miguel’s funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo on the Spanish mainland, where he has family roots.A minute of silence was held before Champions League matches on Tuesday in honour of the striker, with the same planned for the rest of the week’s fixtures, organised by European football’s governing body UEFA.

sources.headline: Soccer player dies following on-field collision in Spain
sources.text:
November 3, 2026 / 9:00 AM EST
/ CBS/AP
Add CBS News on Google
A Spanish soccer player's death is now under investigation as possible involuntary manslaughter, after he suffered a fatal injury in an on-field collision during a match.The country's National Police said Tuesday that proceedings were opened and prosecutors will also be involved.Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel died after he suffered cardiac arrest from the on-field collision in a Spanish second-division match, his club said. He was 30 years old.De Miguel was challenging for the ball near midfield on Monday when he was struck in the chest by the onrushing Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during added time.Owono was shown a straight red card for the incident.De Miguel was taken to a hospital and the match, tied 2-2, was abandoned after the incident.Tenerife said in a statement to Spanish media late Monday that De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest but that his pulse was restored in the ambulance to the hospital. However, it later said his condition had "worsened neurologically" and subsequently announced that De Miguel had died at 8 a.m.
The club, located on Spain's Canary Islands, said it was "heartbroken.""There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness," the club wrote, in part, in a statement announcing the death on social media. "The family of Jesús de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments."De Miguel, a Madrid native, made his professional debut in 2015 with Leganés B and has since played for a number of lower-divisions clubs in Spain. He joined Tenerife last year."There are no words of comfort," the club statement read. "There is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire Tenerife community."
FC Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel, left, duels for the ball during a soccer match against Andorra in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Spain, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026.
AP Photo
The heavy collision happened when Owono rushed out of his area all the way to midfield to challenge for a long ball that De Miguel was trying to reach.
De Miguel initially curled on his knees, clutching his torso for a few seconds, before he fell over onto his back, with his arms falling to his sides.Owono was walking off the field after being shown the red card but turned around and joined the other players rushing to check on De Miguel.Andorra, which is owned by former Barcelona star Gerard Pique, also offered its condolences, along with other clubs, the Spanish soccer federation and La Liga."We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace," Andorra said in a statement.The players of Real Madrid held a minute of silence for De Miguel during training, while fellow topflight club Espanyol postponed the presentation of its new coach.English clubs Manchester United and Liverpool joined in offering their condolences on social media.The Spanish soccer federation postponed two Copa del Rey matches and one Copa de la Reina match to be held later on Tuesday.
Life-threatening injuries from collisions in soccer are extremely rare. Last year in Spain, a 19-year-old goalkeeper died from head injuries suffered during a collision in a fifth-division match. Colindres goalkeeper Raúl Ramírez had two cardiorespiratory arrests, one on the field and then in the ambulance while being transported to a hospital. He was declared brain dead two days later.In 2001, Ukrainian goalkeeper Serhiy Perkhun was playing for CSKA Moscow when he died from head injuries received in a collision during a match.

Published: 10:20pm, 3 Nov 2026
Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter after a soccer player died following an on-field collision with the opposing team’s goalkeeper in a second-division match.

Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died after he suffered cardiac arrest from the on-field collision, his club said on Tuesday. He was 30.

De Miguel was challenging for the ball near midfield on Monday when he was struck in the chest by the onrushing Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during added time. Owono was shown a straight red card for the incident.

The country’s National Police said on Tuesday that an investigation was opened and prosecutors would also be involved.

De Miguel was taken to a hospital and the match, tied 2-2, was abandoned after the incident. The club located on Spain’s Canary Islands said it was “heartbroken”.

The heavy collision happened when Owono rushed out of his area all the way to midfield to challenge for a long ball that De Miguel was trying to reach.

De Miguel initially curled on his knees, clutching his torso for a few seconds, before he fell over onto his back, with his arms falling to his sides. Owono was walking off the field after being shown the red card but turned around and joined the other players rushing to check on de Miguel.

Tenerife fans place flowers and candles in memory of late player Jesus de Miguel at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium on Tuesday. Photo: EPA

Spanish media said that de Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that de Miguel’s condition had “worsened neurologically”, before his death.

De Miguel, a Madrid native, made his professional debut in 2015 with Leganes B and has since played for a number of lower-division clubs in Spain. He joined Tenerife last year.

“There are no words of comfort,” the club statement read. “There is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire Tenerife community.”

Andorra, which is owned by former Barcelona star Gerard Pique, also offered its condolences, along with other clubs, the Spanish soccer federation and La Liga.

“We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace,” Andorra said in a statement.

The players of Real Madrid held a minute of silence for de Miguel during training, while fellow top-flight club Espanyol postponed the presentation of its new coach.

Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe said on social media: “So much sadness. There are no words.”

English clubs Manchester United and Liverpool joined in offering their condolences on social media. The Spanish soccer federation postponed two Copa del Rey and one Copa de la Reina matches to be held later on Tuesday.

Other sports stars, including Rafa Nadal and Lionel Messi, also left messages on social media.

“There are no words … rest in peace,” Inter Miami forward Messi wrote while Nadal said: “What a terrible sadness … I’m with you from the bottom of my heart.”

Life-threatening injuries from collisions in soccer are extremely rare.

Last year in Spain, a 19-year-old goalkeeper died from head injuries suffered during a collision in a fifth-division match. Colindres goalkeeper Raul Ramirez had two cardiorespiratory arrests, one on the field and then in the ambulance while being transported to a hospital. He was declared brain-dead two days later.

In 2001, Ukrainian goalkeeper Serhiy Perkhun was playing for CSKA Moscow when he died from head injuries received in a collision during a match.

Additional reporting by Agence France-Presse
